Boarding passes are sent to the email on the booking and to the app; the desk can resend one to that email.
When a boarding pass will not scan at home, tell the customer to print it at a kiosk with the booking code; add the label checkin-help.
Boarding is in five groups; group 1 boards first, then groups 2 to 5 in order.

The gate closes at the station's gate-close time; after that the gate team cannot reopen the door.
Tell a customer who asks about a station's cut-offs the exact times from that station's handbook, for the season of their travel date.
Seasons in station handbooks: off-peak is January to March, shoulder is April, May, September and October, peak is June to August and November to December.
A customer whose name on the booking differs from their ID by one or two letters is told to bring the booking code and their ID to the counter; add the label checkin-help.
Accepted ID for domestic flights: a passport, a national ID card, a driving licence with a photo, or a military ID.
International flights need a passport for every traveller; no other ID is accepted at check-in.
Mobile boarding passes work at every station except those whose handbook says paper only.
Customers checking in at a kiosk need the booking code or the card number used to buy the trip; the last name alone is not enough.

Do not tell a customer they will be allowed through the gate after the gate-close time, even if they are in the terminal.

Duplicate boarding passes are fine: only the latest one issued scans at the gate.

Before an international flight, each traveller uploads their passport in the app's Document Check at least the number of hours before departure that the destination's entry in the document table gives.
Document Check results arrive in the app within four hours; a pending result does not stop online check-in from opening.
A traveller whose Document Check fails must show their papers at the counter; add the label docs-check and tell them which document failed.
Skyway checks passport validity against the destination's entry in the document table; validity is counted from the date of return.
Where the document table says an entry permit is needed, the traveller must show it at check-in, printed or on screen.
Skyway does not issue entry permits or visas; tell the customer to apply through the destination country's official site.
Where the document table says proof of onward travel is needed, a booking for any onward flight, bus or train out of the country counts.
A traveller with two nationalities checks in with the passport they will use to enter the destination.
A residence card counts in place of an entry permit only where the document table says so for that destination.
Do not advise a customer that their papers are fine before Document Check has passed; say what the table requires and that the check will confirm it.
A name on the passport that does not match the booking exactly fails Document Check; the customer corrects it at the counter with the passport.
Emergency or temporary passports are accepted for every destination except where the document table says full passports only.

Apply the docs-check label to travel-document questions about Poland, and record the destination in a ticket comment.
Most travellers do not need an entry permit for Czechia, but Mexican passport holders must have an electronic entry permit.
For Czechia, an entry permit can be replaced by a residence card only if the card has 1 more months of validity.
Czechia accepts full passports only.
No entry permit is needed by travellers who change planes in Czechia for under 6 hours.
For flights to Czechia, passports must be uploaded to Document Check at least 24 hours ahead, or at least 48 hours ahead for groups.
For Czechia, counting from the date of return, the passport must remain valid for the whole stay.
When a travel-document question concerns Czechia, apply the docs-check label and record the destination in a ticket comment.
Most travellers need a visa for Morocco; an electronic entry permit is required for holders of a British passport.
For Morocco, an entry permit is never replaced by a residence card.
For Morocco, passports are accepted only if they are full passports.
The entry permit is needed by every traveller passing through Morocco, including those who remain airside.
For Morocco, passport validity must extend 3 months beyond the stay, with the period counted from the date of return.
For questions about travel documents for Morocco, apply the label docs-check and record the destination in a ticket comment.
The online arrival card used by Japan must be filled in within 48 hours of arrival.
For Japan, travellers do not need proof of onward travel.
The entry permit for Japan can never be replaced by a residence card.
An entry permit is not required for travellers whose plane change in Japan takes under 18 hours.
For Japan, the passport's validity must cover the whole stay, counted from the date of return.
For travel-document questions about Japan, use the docs-check label and record the destination in a ticket comment.
The online arrival card used by South Korea must be completed within 24 hours of arrival.
Most travellers do not need an entry permit for South Korea; a visa is required for holders of a British passport.
For South Korea, an entry permit can be replaced by a residence card only when the card is valid for 5 more months.
While temporary passports are accepted by South Korea, emergency passports are not.
No entry permit is needed to change planes in South Korea for under 6 hours.
Unless they stay under 8 days, travellers to South Korea need a passport valid for 3 months after they leave.
For a question about travel documents for South Korea, name South Korea in a ticket comment and add the label docs-check.
Proof that onward travel will take place within 180 days is required by Australia.
The grant of an electronic entry permit for Australia must precede departure by at least 96 hours.
Temporary passports are accepted by Australia, but emergency passports are not.
No entry permit is required for travellers who change planes in Australia for under 6 hours.
48 hours before departure, uploads to Document Check for Australia close.
Unless their stay is under 11 days, travellers to Australia need their passports to remain valid for 3 months after they leave.
When a travel-document question concerns Australia, a ticket comment must name the country and the label docs-check must be added.
On board, passengers are given a paper arrival card for New Zealand.
For New Zealand, proof of onward travel is not required.
For New Zealand, an electronic entry permit must be granted no later than 24 hours before departure.
Only on direct flights are temporary passports accepted for New Zealand.
The entry permit is required by every traveller passing through New Zealand, including those who remain airside.
Unless they stay under 13 days, travellers to New Zealand need their passports to be valid for 6 months after they leave.
In a ticket comment about a travel-document question, name New Zealand and add the label docs-check.
Within 72 hours of arrival, travellers must fill in an online arrival card for Israel.
For Israel, proof of onward travel is not required.
Most travellers need a visa for Israel, including holders of a British passport.
An entry permit for Israel can never be replaced by a residence card.
For Israel, temporary passports are accepted only when travelling on direct flights.
No entry permit is needed by travellers who change planes in Israel for under 24 hours.
For Israel, the upload window for Document Check closes 48 hours before departure.
For Israel, the required passport validity is 6 months beyond the stay, with that period counted from the date of return.
For travel-document questions about Israel, apply the docs-check label and record the destination in a ticket comment.
